newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia criticises Japan move on national car.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia criticises Japan move on national car.

text.p: Indonesian State Secretary Murdiono said on Monday that President Suharto had expressed disappointment over Japan's proposed move to bring Jakarta's controversial national car programme to the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

"Indonesia is disappointed with Japan's attitude, which does not accomodate our interests," Murdiono said, adding that Suharto had instructed officials to cease bilateral talks with Japan on the national car issue.
Murdiono told reporters at the state palace that Suharto had decided the national car programme would continue despite Japan's intended move.
A Japanese Trade Ministry official said last week Japan will ask the WTO to create a panel to rule on its complaint over Indonesia's car policy.
He said it will request that a panel be formed at the next meeting of the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body on April 30.

Indonesia's national car policy gives PT Timor Putra Nasional, controlled by President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra, tax and tariff breaks to produce the Timor car in association with Kia Motors Corp of South Korea.
Along with Japan, the United States and the European Union have also complained about the programme, which they say has given Timor Putra an unfair price advantage in the automobile market.
